title: Object-Oriented Programming Basics
description: Understand classes, objects, inheritance, and encapsulation — the core of OOP.

concepts.example_text: Object-Oriented Programming organizes code around 'objects' that model real things. A Dog object has properties (name, breed, age) and behaviors (bark, fetch, sit). Instead of scattered variables and functions, OOP bundles related data and logic together into a single unit.

A class is a blueprint; an object is a thing built from that blueprint. The class 'Car' defines that cars have a color and can drive. The object 'myCar' is a specific red car. You can create many objects from one class — like building many houses from the same floor plan.

1) Encapsulation — bundling data and methods together, hiding internal details. 2) Inheritance — creating new classes based on existing ones. 3) Polymorphism — different classes responding to the same method differently. 4) Abstraction — simplifying complex systems by exposing only what's needed.

terms.definition: A blueprint or template that defines the properties (data) and methods (behavior) that objects of that type will have.
A specific thing created from a class. It has actual values for the properties defined in the class.
A special method that runs when a new object is created. It initializes the object's properties with starting values.
A mechanism where a new class (child) inherits properties and methods from an existing class (parent). Promotes code reuse.
Hiding an object's internal data and only exposing it through controlled methods (getters/setters). Protects data integrity.
A function that belongs to a class. It defines what objects of that class can do.

questions.question: What is the relationship between a class and an object?
options: A class is an instance of an object
An object is an instance of a class
A class is a type of function
questions.explanation: A class is a blueprint that defines properties and methods. An object is a specific instance created from that blueprint with actual values.

questions.question: What does a constructor do?
options: Initializes a new object with starting values
questions.explanation: A constructor is a special method that runs automatically when you create a new object. It sets up the object's initial state.

questions.question: What is inheritance in OOP?
options: A child class gaining properties/methods from a parent class
Two objects sharing the same variable
questions.explanation: Inheritance lets a new class extend an existing class, automatically gaining its properties and methods while adding its own.

questions.question: Why is encapsulation important?
options: It protects data from invalid changes
questions.explanation: Encapsulation hides internal data behind controlled methods. A BankAccount can prevent negative deposits by validating inside the deposit() method.

questions.question: In 'class Cat extends Animal', what is Cat?
questions.explanation: Cat is the child class (subclass) that extends (inherits from) Animal, the parent class. Cat gets all of Animal's properties and methods.
